source: evidence/upstream/capability-snapshot.md (engineering docs/capabilities/snapshot-2026-10-23b.md, draft 3) sections 8 and 9; website reference/claims.json; engineering docs/DECISIONS.md D-019..D-031
rule: Every public sentence about the product maps to one claim id below and keeps its qualifier beside it. Labels: verified = Verified reality on the named hardware; scope = committed engineering scope, not built; direction = strategic hypothesis, always introduced as direction. observation = a dated event from a committed engineering record, allowed by the owner's voice direction of 2026-11-06. It makes no capability, reliability or platform claim, generalizes to nothing, names no machine or person, and never covers running one model across devices.

no-release.label: verified
no-release.text: UCompute is in development. There is no public release or download yet.

run-local.label: verified
run-local.text: UCompute Run runs small open models on your own computer, with no account and no UCompute service. By default, your requests stay on your device.
run-local.qualifier: Demonstrated on an Apple M2 Mac (macOS 26.2) and a Windows 11 laptop with an Intel Arc 140V GPU; both platforms are experimental; other platforms are not yet available, and most are planned. Downloading a model or the engine uses the internet.

catalog-fit.label: verified
catalog-fit.text: Before you download a model, UCompute shows its size, its license and whether it fits in your computer's memory. Every download is checked against a pinned SHA-256 hash.
catalog-fit.qualifier: Demonstrated on an Apple M2 Mac (macOS 26.2); the platform is experimental. Memory-fit estimates are calibrated for Apple Silicon Macs.

openai-clients.label: verified
openai-clients.text: UCompute's local API works with the official OpenAI Python and JavaScript client libraries; only the base URL changes.
openai-clients.qualifier: Demonstrated on an Apple M2 Mac (macOS 26.2); the platform is experimental. Chat and completions with streaming; tool calling is not yet verified.

mesh-pair-choose.label: verified
mesh-pair-choose.text: UCompute Mesh lets you pair your own devices with a short code and choose which one runs a request. Each request runs whole on one device; UCompute does not split a model across devices.
mesh-pair-choose.qualifier: Tested with development builds between one Apple M2 Mac and one Windows 11 laptop (Intel Arc 140V) on the same Wi-Fi network or phone hotspot, and between that Mac and one Linux desktop computer (Ubuntu, processor only, a development build of the background program compiled and started by hand; no app or installer) on a home Wi-Fi network. Linux is a planned platform, not a supported one. Pairing between two Macs is not yet shown to work. Since 2026-11-06 Growth omits the closing clause 'UCompute does not split a model across devices': a development build ran one model across two machines that day. The clause stays in this entry until Website's claims change. 'Each request runs whole on one device' stands for Mesh requests.

demo-2026-10-19.label: verified
demo-2026-10-19.text: In a test on 19 October 2026 (UTC), development builds of the desktop app on a MacBook Air (Apple M2, macOS 26.2) and a Windows 11 laptop (Intel Core Ultra 7 258V, Arc 140V) were paired through their own windows on one phone hotspot, and the Windows app ran a prompt on the Mac (the Mac's permission for the laptop to run prompts was set through the Mac's local API, not its window). A request in the other direction, sent through the Mac's local API rather than its app window, ran on the laptop's GPU. Each request ran whole on one device; no model was split. The test model was a 15-million-parameter fixture, so speeds from it are not performance figures.

transport.label: verified
transport.text: Traffic between paired devices is encrypted and both ends are authenticated: QUIC with TLS 1.3 and device keys pinned at pairing. Your device will not send work to a device you have not paired.
transport.qualifier: If a page says how the encryption was checked, add: The check that captured traffic carries no readable prompt text ran on one computer. The sentence 'A device you have not paired cannot send you work' carries its own qualifier: Tested with several instances on one computer, not yet between two machines.

local-only.label: verified
local-only.text: Your prompts and responses stay on your device unless you pair another device and choose to run a request there. Local-only mode refuses every off-device request.
local-only.qualifier: Downloading a model or the engine uses the internet.

revocation.label: verified
revocation.text: You can revoke a paired device at any time. In our two-machine tests, its connection closed less than a tenth of a second after the revoke (between 0.002 s and 0.061 s in four runs), and its next request was refused.
revocation.qualifier: Never say what the revoked device is told.

audit.label: verified
audit.text: Audit logs record each off-device request without the prompt or the response.

device-sees-prompt.label: verified
device-sees-prompt.text: The device that runs your request processes your prompt. Pair only devices you control or trust.
device-sees-prompt.qualifier: Required context whenever transport or local-only is described.

platforms.label: verified
platforms.text: No platform is declared supported yet. macOS 26.2 on Apple M2 and Windows 11 on an Intel Core Ultra 7 258V with Arc 140V are experimental; Linux, other GPUs and phones (as clients) are planned.

planned.label: scope
planned.text: Planned, with no date: running one model across several devices, an opt-in open network (UCompute Swarm), compute credits and an optional managed service (UCompute Cloud). None of these exists today.
planned.qualifier: Since 2026-11-06 do not write 'None of these exists today' or 'does not exist today' about running one model across devices; say it is planned, with no date, and is not a feature.
planned.evidence: snapshot 8.13; F-03-*, U-05 NOT_STARTED; ADR-0005 Proposed

direction.label: direction
direction.text: Our direction: Compute better. Together. Use your own compute for free. Share compute to earn credits. Let trusted people use your hardware for free. Spend credits to access compensated compute. Purchase credits when you need more. Share your compute. Not your computer.
direction.qualifier: Introduce with 'Our direction:' or 'What we are building toward:'. Add: Credits do not exist yet. Free does not mean unlimited. Never next to download, sign-up or 'available' wording.

license.label: verified
license.text: UCompute's code is licensed under Apache-2.0. The source has not been published yet.

connect-by-address.label: verified
connect-by-address.text: Where a network blocks automatic discovery, as some campus Wi-Fi does, paired devices can still connect by address. An address alone is never trusted: the device must present the key it was paired with.
connect-by-address.qualifier: Reconnecting by address was shown between one Mac and one Windows laptop on the same campus network, with development builds.

windows-firewall.label: verified
windows-firewall.text: On Windows, UCompute asks before it lets your paired devices reach it through the firewall, and the rule it adds covers only its own program, on private networks.
windows-firewall.qualifier: Shown in October 2026 on one Windows 11 laptop with a development build (later builds not yet re-checked); Windows asks for administrator approval.

private-alpha.label: verified
private-alpha.text: A private alpha build for macOS on Apple Silicon exists for an owner-managed cohort. It is not a public release and is not open for sign-up.
private-alpha.qualifier: Never name testers or their number, never link the file, never describe the cohort as open. Source: D-031 (2026-10-30), website LAUNCH.md.

engine.label: verified
engine.text: UCompute runs models through a pinned release of llama.cpp (MIT), downloaded on first use and verified against a pinned SHA-256 hash (the digest published for that release); UCompute does not write its own inference kernels.

audit-detail.label: verified
audit-detail.text: The audit trail is a file of JSON lines with a timestamp, an event kind, the other device's id and structured fields (ids, sizes, reasons, durations). The writer refuses fields named prompt, content, messages, api_key, private_key or pkcs8 and any string over 2 KiB; the file rotates at 8 MiB with three rotated files kept and an audit_rotated line that states the dropped bytes; owner actions and revocations are copied to a separately rotated security trail; refused-connection lines are capped at 20 per minute with the rest counted.
audit-detail.qualifier: Mechanics held by automated tests on one computer (development build, October 2026); the absence of prompt text in the logs was checked in the two-machine runs (claim audit). On Windows the files carry the profile folder's access rights; second-account access is untested.
audit-detail.evidence: engineering ADR-0003 section 9.11; crates/ucompute-observability; THREAT_MODEL M3-26, M3-27, M3-28, M3-08; snapshot 3.2 audit row, 3.3 F-06-01 row

download-integrity.label: verified
download-integrity.text: UCompute's catalog pins each model to a SHA-256 hash and to the repository revision it is downloaded from. A download whose bytes do not match is rejected and the partial file deleted; a plain http:// URL is refused before any request is made; an interrupted download continues from where it stopped when you start it again; and a model already on disk is hashed again against its manifest each time the engine loads it, so a mismatch stops the load before the engine starts.
download-integrity.qualifier: Demonstrated on an Apple M2 Mac (macOS 26.2) with development builds, October 2026; the platform is experimental. A matching hash proves the bytes are the ones the catalog pinned; it does not prove who trained the model or that its contents are safe.
download-integrity.evidence: snapshot 2026-10-23b section 3.1 row 'Verified model downloads' (F-01-05, F-05-01, F-05-02, F-05-04; ca298bd; Mac-M2); engineering docs/VERIFICATION.md F-01-05 (corrupted_byte_is_rejected_and_partial_deleted, http_url_refused_before_any_network, cut_at_half_then_resume, tampered_blob_is_integrity_mismatch_before_any_spawn); engineering README (catalog: revision + SHA-256 + license)

pairing-code.label: verified
pairing-code.text: Pairing uses a six-digit code that works once and is valid for 120 seconds, checked with a SPAKE2 exchange. The device handles one attempt at a time, and the sixth failure within 60 seconds closes the pairing endpoint for that window.
pairing-code.qualifier: Describes development builds, October 2026. A QR variant replaces the code with a one-time secret. Requirement F-02-02 is VERIFIED in the ledger; the wording sits in a design record, not in Website's claims.json, and is in Website's review queue (handoffs/2026-11-06-website-link-and-claim-review.md).
pairing-code.evidence: engineering docs/decisions/ADR-0003-peer-transport-and-pairing.md (mirrored), section 3 'Code' and section 9 steps; docs/REQUIREMENTS.csv F-02-02 VERIFIED

obs-keepalive.label: observation
obs-keepalive.text: Burst requests to llama-server failed at about 0.5% with 'connection closed before message completed'. The daemon's client was reusing idle connections the engine had already closed. With no reuse: 0 failures in 43,092 admitted requests across two runs. Why llama-server closes them is not determined.
obs-keepalive.qualifier: One test machine, development build, October 2026. Reproduced by a second, independent run with and without the fix. The link to the earlier soak's 0.51% is inferred, so never say this explains the soak.

obs-soak-kills.label: observation
obs-soak-kills.text: A 24-hour soak sends the engine SIGKILL every 50 cycles. In the third soak there were 2,607 kills, each recovered within a second.
obs-soak-kills.qualifier: One test machine, development build, 2026-10-31/11-01; the soak passed with documented interference.

obs-soak-miss.label: observation
obs-soak-miss.text: The second 24-hour soak failed by its own rule: 2 requests out of 5.3 million got no answer and no typed error, with the engine alive. The better-fitting reading is that the test client's clock ran out before the daemon's own timeout could answer. That reading is not established.
obs-soak-miss.qualifier: One test machine, development build, October 2026. Always say it is unproven.

obs-wifi-drop.label: observation
obs-wifi-drop.text: A test machine dropped off the local network overnight without rebooting, more than once. The likely cause is Ubuntu's default Wi-Fi power saving, which was turned off on 2026-10-29. An Ethernet cable is the fallback.
obs-wifi-drop.qualifier: Likely, not proven. Never name the machine or say the problem is gone.

obs-dev-mac.label: observation
obs-dev-mac.text: Development and many tests run on a MacBook Air (Apple M2) with 8 GB of unified memory.
obs-dev-mac.evidence: capability snapshot 2026-10-23b, hardware list; P1 preflight record (little free memory after a release build)

obs-spake2.label: observation
obs-spake2.text: Pairing uses the spake2 crate 0.4.0, which is three years old, unaudited and by its own description probably not constant-time. It protects a one-time, 120-second secret; long-term security rests on TLS 1.3 and pinned keys. A newer release is being tracked.
obs-spake2.qualifier: Design record and Cargo.lock at engineering HEAD on 2026-11-06. Re-check the version before posting.

split-design.label: scope
split-design.text: The engineering design for splitting one model between two devices keeps both ends of the RPC connection on loopback and carries the bytes inside the existing authenticated connection between the paired devices. It is a design under test, not a feature.
split-design.qualifier: Say nothing about any run or result until a VERIFIED ledger row and an updated claims.json exist, or the owner releases it.
split-design.evidence: engineering ADR-0005 (Proposed); public since 2026-10-30 in the RPC note; F-03-01 IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED

numbers.rule: A number appears only with its model, its hardware, a plain-language build qualifier ('development build, October 2026') and, for tokens per second, the words 'path check, not performance'.

memory estimate within -4.6 % to +8.9 % of measured, 14 combinations

burst failure rate before and after, obs-keepalive
